source.title: Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors
source.authors: Yuxiao Li; Alina Fastowski; Efstratios Zaradoukas; Bardh Prenkaj; Gjergji Kasneci

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study constructs a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction, then tests a different intervention: removing that direction's projection from behavior-steering vectors and measuring changes in jailbreak ASR. This is not the original intervention that projects the direction out of residual activations at every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The paper reports tests of removing the refusal-aligned component from steering vectors and regression analyses relating refusal-direction cosine similarity to steering-induced ASR slopes. Those results are included below. The direction-selection bypass, induce, and KL scores are used to select the direction, so they are not recorded as results. General-capability benchmarks under unrelated behavior steering are not rows because they do not test the refusal-direction intervention. The paper also reports refusal rates on benign prompts for unrelated behavior vectors, but provides those only in a figure and does not add or remove the refusal direction itself.
record.test_reason: The study builds the Arditi-style difference-in-means refusal direction on six chat models. It then intervenes on it in a different way: it projects that direction out of CAA steering vectors and measures the change in jailbreak ASR. It also regresses ASR slope on each steering vector's cosine with the direction. Both results bear on whether the direction mediates refusal (V1). The finding that removing it leaves most of the steering effect bears on V4. The main question is steering safety, so the evidence is indirect.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that steering vectors' overlap with the refusal direction predicts their effect on jailbreak ASR. Ablating the refusal-aligned component mitigates but does not eliminate that effect. They attribute the residual to a multidimensional safety subspace and/or to refusal components regenerated downstream.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal directions following the original work, but uses a selected direction to remove projections from behavior-steering vectors rather than ablating the refusal direction directly from residual activations at all layers and positions or adding it to induce refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: The relation between refusal-direction alignment and ASR slope differs by model: the prefix-injection regression for Qwen 3B is not statistically significant (p-value = 0.696), while the other listed models have p-value <0.001. The size of the ablation reduction also varies by model and attack setting.
record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be publicly released but gives no URL.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: A single run with greedy decoding is used unless otherwise stated. The refusal direction is a one-dimensional proxy selected on validation scores. Ablation is applied to the behavior-steering vectors, not to residual activations throughout the model. The reported ablation metric averages across steering behaviors and multipliers, and uncertainty estimates for those ASR reductions are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the included regression and ablation results. The general-capability MMLU and TriviaQA results under behavior steering are not included because they do not test capability under refusal-direction ablation. The benign-prompt FRR curves are not included because they concern unrelated behavior-steering vectors rather than adding or removing the refusal direction.

untested.parts: Direct ablation of the direction from residual activations at all layers and positions. Direct addition of the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. Capability preservation under refusal-direction intervention (the MMLU/TriviaQA results are for behaviour steering only).
No explicit affine, cone or multi-direction model is fitted or compared. Residual effects could also come from refusal components regenerated downstream, as the authors note.
No weight edit or abliterated model.
Prompt jailbreaks are not analysed for suppression of the direction; no adversarial training.

missing.what: Benign-prompt false refusal rate for steering vectors at opposite ends of refusal-direction alignment. Anti-LGBTQ (positively aligned) has FRR slope +3.589; Self-Awareness (negatively aligned) has slope −2.893. This is an induce-refusal-on-harmless analogue for V1.
Per-behaviour pre/post-ablation ΔASR for Anti-LGBTQ and Self-Awareness across Qwen sizes, with reductions up to 86%. These show behaviour-dependent ablation effects larger than the Table 2 means.

record.verdict_notes: The regression rows were wrongly marked cannot_determine. They are readable associations, and the steering does add the aligned component, so they bear on V1's add side, though confounded by the vectors' other components. The direction-selection scores (bypass, induce, KL) were correctly excluded. The single-run greedy decoding and GPT-4o-mini judge are noted in the record's problems field.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not ablate the refusal direction directly from residual activations at every layer and position, or add that direction to induce harmless refusals. Capability preservation is not tested under the refusal-direction-component ablation.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.

The attacks are prompt-level jailbreaks combined with behavior steering; the study does not test whether they work by suppressing the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.

The study does not compare affine, cone, or other explicit multidimensional refusal representations. It tests whether removing one refusal-aligned component fully removes steering-induced safety perturbations.
No separate harmfulness-judgment representation and refusal-decision representation are tested.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other transfer of the refusal direction is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or training stages is performed.

relationships.condition: Regression of ASR slope on cosine with the refusal direction, all models and attacks except Qwen 3B prefix injection
relationships.reason: Steering vectors aligned with the direction lower ASR, and anti-aligned vectors raise it (r −0.78 to −0.99, R² 0.61–0.98). This is correlational. See r20–r36.
relationships.display_finding: Alignment with the refusal direction correlated with lower attack-success slopes and anti-alignment with higher slopes, with correlations from −0.78 to −0.99 and R² from 0.61 to 0.98.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Regression of ASR slope on cosine with the refusal direction, all models and attacks except Qwen 3B prefix injection
source_check.reason: Tables 1, 6 and 7: r from −0.78 to −0.99, R² from 0.61 to 0.98, all p < 0.05. Vectors aligned with r-hat lower ASR, which fits the add/induce side. FRR in Figure 6 agrees. Correlational, with about 9 vectors per model.

relationships.reason: No relation between alignment and ASR slope (p = 0.696, r19). Ablation reduces the effect by only 2.21% (r2).
relationships.display_finding: Alignment was unrelated to attack-success slope, with p=0.696, and ablation reduced the effect by only 2.21%.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Table 1: r = 0.15, p = 0.696. Table 2: only a 2.21% reduction. Steering barely moves ASR in this setting (mean |ΔASR| 1.43), so the null may reflect little variance to explain rather than a failure of the direction.

relationships.condition: Projecting the direction out of steering vectors, six models × three attacks
relationships.reason: Removing the refusal-direction component cuts mean steering-induced |ΔASR| by only 2–25%. Most of the steering effect on refusal passes through other components. See r1–r18.
relationships.display_finding: Removing the refusal-direction component reduced mean steering-induced absolute attack-success changes by only 2–25%, leaving most of the effect intact.

relationships.display_finding: After projection, 75–98% of the absolute steering-induced ASR change remained, consistent with either multidimensional safety structure or downstream regeneration.

relation.reason: Its own results (Tables 1, 2, 6, 7) bear on the direction's causal role. It does not merely use the direction as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study builds the Arditi DiM direction with the original selection protocol, then tests it with different methods: a cosine-vs-ASR-slope regression, and projecting r-hat out of the steering vectors rather than out of activations. Its results bear on whether r-hat carries refusal effects. T3 (new setting: CAA behaviour steering) is a close alternative.

source_check.notes: The ablation projects r-hat out of the steering vectors only, at one layer, not out of activations at every layer as Arditi does. Table 2 comes from a single greedy run with no uncertainty and no random-direction projection control, so controls=y and uncertainty=y fit only the regressions. Table 6 and 7 cells were placed by model order and the B.2 ranges; the B.2 claim of R² ≳ 0.88 conflicts with Gemma's 0.64.

statements.correction: Table 2: projecting r-hat out of CAA steering vectors before adding them at the steering layer (not out of activations at every layer) cuts mean |ΔASR| by 2.21–25.27% over 6 models × 3 attacks. Qwen 3B prefix injection: 1.43→1.40 (2.21%). Llama 7B prompt-only: 1.54→1.16 (25.27%). The authors give two explanations for the residual: a multidimensional safety subspace, or refusal components regenerated downstream. They list a higher-dimensional analysis as future work. r19: Qwen 3B prefix-injection regression, γ1 = 1.46, r = 0.15, p = 0.696.
statements.problem: The numbers for this study are right: 2–25%, six models, three attacks, 1.43→1.40, 1.54→1.16. But citing it for 'refusal effects are not confined to one direction' overstates the result. The study removes r-hat only from the steering vector, at one layer, and the authors give downstream regeneration as an equally possible explanation. r19 is cited but not described. The Gemma-7B-it, Ornith, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-Coder and Llama-3-70B figures are not from this study.
